2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
3	# horizontally centered against the system info column.
4	set -euo pipefail

17	FAVORITES=(
18	)

20	
21	# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
22	# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
23	# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
24	# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
25	# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
26	# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
27	# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
28	# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
29	# (uncentered).
30	POKEMON_WIDTH=
31	
32	# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
33	# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
34	# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
35	# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
36	CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
37	
38	# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
39	# text, on top of the centering above.
40	POKEMON_GAP=2
41	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
42	
43	FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"
44	
45	sprite="$(mktemp)"
46	padded="$(mktemp)"
47	trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT
48	
49	if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
50	    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
51	    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
52	else
53	    args=("groudon")
54	fi
55	
56	pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"
57	
58	sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
59	sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
60	info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)
61	
62	default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
63	width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"
64	
65	pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))

68	fi
69

71	if (( pad_left < 0 )); then

73	fi

86	}

90	    --logo-type file-raw \
91	    --logo "$padded" \
92	    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
93	    --logo-padding-right "$POKEMON_GAP"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
# text, on top of the centering above.
POKEMON_GAP=2
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
# text, on top of the centering above.
POKEMON_GAP=2
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-right "$POKEMON_GAP"

lines: # square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.

-# text, on top of the centering above.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
3	# horizontally centered against the system info column.
4	set -euo pipefail
5	
6	# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
7	# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
8	#          script are ignored)
9	# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
10	USE_FAVORITES=false
11	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
12	
13	# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
14	# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
15	# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
16	# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
17	FAVORITES=(
18	)
19	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
20

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

aiTitle: Remove pokemon gap feature and allow column gap customization

content.text: That means dropping the mechanism that keeps the info column starting at a fixed spot regardless of which pokemon is drawn (documented at the top of the script) — the right edge will now hug whatever sprite is drawn instead of a fixed column boundary. Since only `groudon` is currently hardcoded (`USE_FAVORITES=false`), that tradeoff won't be visible today, but it would matter if you ever flip on `FAVORITES`. I'll make the change and update the comments to reflect it.

input.old_string:
# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
input.new_string:
# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

+# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
+# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
+# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.

# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and

set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \

    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

aiTitle: Remove pokemon gap feature and allow column gap customization

content.text:
The change works — the info text now starts right after the sprite's own bounding box on each row (via `sprite_width`) instead of a wider fixed column, with `pad_left` still centering the sprite as before.

Summary of changes in `/home/krubics/.local/bin/pokefetch`:
- Removed `POKEMON_GAP` (was a hardcoded `--logo-padding-right` of 2).
- Changed the right-pad calculation from padding to the full centering `$width` down to padding only to `$sprite_width`, so text hugs the sprite's actual right edge.
- Updated the `POKEMON_WIDTH` comment to reflect it now only controls centering, not text distance.

Note: this means the info column start is no longer fixed across different pokemon (only matters if you ever enable `FAVORITES`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

}

content.content:
Display pokemon sprites in your terminal.

Usage: pokeget [OPTIONS] [POKEMON]...

Arguments:
  [POKEMON]...  The pokemon to display, use "random" to get a random pokemon, use a region to get a random pokemon from that region

Options:
      --hide-name    Whether to hide the pokemon's name which appears above it
  -f, --form <FORM>  The form of the pokemon [default: ""]
  -m, --mega         Display the pokemon as it's mega form
      --mega-x       Display the pokemon as it's mega X form
      --mega-y       Display the pokemon as it's mega Y form
  -s, --shiny        Display the pokemon as shiny
  -a, --alolan       Display the alolan variant of the pokemon
  -g, --gmax         Display the gigantamax variant of the pokemon
      --hisui        Display the hisui variant of the pokemon
  -n, --noble        Display the noble variant of the pokemon, this option often times only works in tandom with --hisui
      --galar        Display the galarian variant of the pokemon
      --female       Display the female variant of the pokemon if it exists. This doesn't apply to nidoran, for some reason
  -h, --help         Print help
  -V, --version      Print version

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this

# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the sprite's own right edge
# and the info text. 0 means the text starts right after the sprite.
POKEMON_GAP=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

    pad_top=0

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))

    pad_left=0
fi

# sprite's own bounding box plus the configured gap, so the info text
# starts that far after the sprite instead of at the wider centering
# column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" -v gap="$POKEMON_GAP" '
{
    stripped = $0

    rightpad = spritewidth + gap - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")

# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the sprite's own right edge
# and the info text. 0 means the text starts right after the sprite.
POKEMON_GAP=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

# exactly $sprite_width + $POKEMON_GAP visible columns wide - i.e. the
# sprite's own bounding box plus the configured gap, so the info text
# starts that far after the sprite instead of at the wider centering
# column.

    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth + gap - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Visible columns to crop off the right edge of every sprite row
# before any width/centering math runs, in case pokeget's own artwork
# has more blank margin on the right than you want. 0 leaves the
# sprite untouched.
POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $sprite_width + $POKEMON_GAP visible columns wide - i.e. the
# sprite's own bounding box plus the configured gap, so the info text
# starts that far after the sprite instead of at the wider centering
# column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" -v gap="$POKEMON_GAP" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth + gap - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Visible columns to crop off the right edge of every sprite row
# before any width/centering math runs, in case pokeget's own artwork
# has more blank margin on the right than you want. 0 leaves the
# sprite untouched.
POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trimmed="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$trimmed" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Visible columns to crop off the right edge of every sprite row
# before any width/centering math runs, in case pokeget's own artwork
# has more blank margin on the right than you want. 0 leaves the
# sprite untouched.
POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trimmed="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$trimmed" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

# Crop POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT visible columns off the right of every row,
# skipping over ANSI color codes so escape sequences stay attached to
# the character they color.
perl -e '
    my $trim = shift;
    while (my $line = <STDIN>) {
        chomp $line;
        my @cols;
        while ($line =~ /\G((?:\x1b\[[0-9;]*m)*[^\x1b])/gc) {
            push @cols, $1;
        }
        splice(@cols, -$trim) if $trim > 0 && @cols;
        print join("", @cols), "\n";
    }
' "$POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT" < "$sprite" > "$trimmed"
mv "$trimmed" "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
3	# horizontally centered against the system info column.
4	set -euo pipefail
5	
6	# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
7	# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
8	#          script are ignored)
9	# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
10	USE_FAVORITES=false
11	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
12	
13	# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
14	# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
15	# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
16	# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
17	FAVORITES=(
18	)
19	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
20	
21	# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
22	# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
23	# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
24	# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
25	# how close the text sits to the sprite.
26	# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
27	# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
28	# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
29	# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
30	# (uncentered).
31	POKEMON_WIDTH=
32	
33	# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
34	# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
35	# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
36	# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
37	CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
38	
39	# Visible columns to crop off the right edge of every sprite row
40	# before any width/centering math runs, in case pokeget's own artwork
41	# has more blank margin on the right than you want. 0 leaves the
42	# sprite untouched.
43	POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT=0
44	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	
46	FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"
47	
48	sprite="$(mktemp)"
49	trimmed="$(mktemp)"
50	padded="$(mktemp)"
51	trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$trimmed" "$padded"' EXIT
52	
53	if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
54	    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
55	    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
56	else
57	    args=("groudon")
58	fi
59	
60	pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"
61	
62	# Crop POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT visible columns off the right of every row,
63	# skipping over ANSI color codes so escape sequences stay attached to
64	# the character they color.
65	perl -CSD -e '
66	    my $trim = shift;
67	    while (my $line = <STDIN>) {
68	        chomp $line;
69	        my @cols;
70	        while ($line =~ /\G((?:\x1b\[[0-9;]*m)*[^\x1b])/gc) {
71	            push @cols, $1;
72	        }
73	        splice(@cols, -$trim) if $trim > 0 && @cols;
74	        print join("", @cols), "\n";
75	    }
76	' "$POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT" < "$sprite" > "$trimmed"
77	mv "$trimmed" "$sprite"
78	
79	sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
80	sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
81	info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)
82	
83	default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
84	width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"
85	
86	pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
87	if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
88	    pad_top=0
89	fi
90	
91	pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
92	if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
93	    pad_left=0
94	fi
95	
96	# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
97	# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
98	# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
99	# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
100	# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.
101	awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" '
102	{
103	    stripped = $0
104	    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
105	    rightpad = spritewidth - length(stripped)
106	    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
107	    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
108	}
109	' "$sprite" > "$padded"
110	
111	fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
112	    --logo-type file-raw \
113	    --logo "$padded" \
114	    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"
115

# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is

)

# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.

# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which

# (uncentered).

# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
# text, on top of the centering above.
POKEMON_GAP=2
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-right "$POKEMON_GAP"

# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) used to horizontally center the sprite.
# The info text starts right after the sprite's own right edge, not
# at this width - so this only controls left/right centering, not
# how close the text sits to the sprite.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Visible columns to crop off the right edge of every sprite row
# before any width/centering math runs, in case pokeget's own artwork
# has more blank margin on the right than you want. 0 leaves the
# sprite untouched.
POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trimmed="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$trimmed" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("random")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

# Crop POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT visible columns off the right of every row,
# skipping over ANSI color codes so escape sequences stay attached to
# the character they color.
perl -CSD -e '
    my $trim = shift;
    while (my $line = <STDIN>) {
        chomp $line;
        my @cols;
        while ($line =~ /\G((?:\x1b\[[0-9;]*m)*[^\x1b])/gc) {
            push @cols, $1;
        }
        splice(@cols, -$trim) if $trim > 0 && @cols;
        print join("", @cols), "\n";
    }
' "$POKEMON_TRIM_RIGHT" < "$sprite" > "$trimmed"
mv "$trimmed" "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $sprite_width visible columns wide - i.e. only up to the
# sprite's own bounding box, so the info text starts right after the
# sprite instead of at the wider centering column.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v spritewidth="$sprite_width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = spritewidth - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
# text, on top of the centering above.
POKEMON_GAP=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-right "$POKEMON_GAP"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5

# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
# text, on top of the centering above.
POKEMON_GAP=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("groudon")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

lastPrompt: Why does fastfetch fall back to 4 columns of padding?

aiTitle: Remove pokemon gap feature and allow column gap customization

content.text:
It's just a built-in default fastfetch ships with — the CLI metadata doesn't expose a stated rationale (unlike many other flags, this one has no documented `default` value, it's baked into the C source). Practically, it's just breathing room: fastfetch's built-in ASCII logos (Arch, Ubuntu, etc.) typically don't have blank trailing columns of their own, so without some right padding the info text would butt right up against the last visible logo column and look cramped — 4 columns is just their chosen amount of spacing for that case.

It's not something specific to pokefetch or your sprite; pokefetch just inherits that default whenever the `--logo-padding-right` flag isn't passed.
