1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
     3	# horizontally centered against the system info column.
     4	set -euo pipefail
     5	
     6	# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
     7	# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
     8	#          script are ignored)
     9	# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
    10	USE_FAVORITES=false
    11	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    12	
    13	# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
    14	# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
    15	# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
    16	# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
    17	FAVORITES=(
    18	)
    19	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    20	
    21	# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
    22	# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
    23	# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
    24	# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
    25	# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
    26	# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
    27	# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
    28	# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
    29	# (uncentered).
    30	POKEMON_WIDTH=
    31	
    32	# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
    33	# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
    34	# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
    35	# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
    36	CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
    37	
    38	# Extra columns of blank space between the pokemon column and the info
    39	# text, on top of the centering above.
    40	POKEMON_GAP=0
    41	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    42	
    43	FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"
    44	
    45	sprite="$(mktemp)"
    46	padded="$(mktemp)"
    47	trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT
    48	
    49	if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    50	    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    51	    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
    52	else
    53	    args=("random")
    54	fi
    55	
    56	pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"
    57	
    58	sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
    59	sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
    60	info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)
    61	
    62	default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
    63	width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$default_width}"
    64	
    65	pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
    66	if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    67	    pad_top=0
    68	fi
    69	
    70	pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
    71	if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    72	    pad_left=0
    73	fi
    74	
    75	# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
    76	# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
    77	# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
    78	# particular row.
    79	awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
    80	{
    81	    stripped = $0
    82	    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    83	    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    84	    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    85	    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
    86	}
    87	' "$sprite" > "$padded"
    88	
    89	fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    90	    --logo-type file-raw \
    91	    --logo "$padded" \
    92	    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    93	    --logo-padding-right "$POKEMON_GAP"

lastPrompt: What happens when is the pokemon larger then the text content?

aiTitle: Remove pokemon gap feature and allow column gap customization

content.text:
Two different things happen depending on which dimension is "larger":

**Taller sprite** (`sprite_lines > info_lines`, more sprite rows than info-text rows):
`pad_top = (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2` goes negative and gets clamped to `0` (line 65-68) — no top padding is added, the sprite starts flush with row 1. Since fastfetch's `--logo-print-remaining` defaults to `true`, the extra sprite rows past the last line of text just print by themselves below the text, left-aligned in the pokemon column with nothing next to them on the right.

**Wider sprite** (`sprite_width > width`, sprite wider than the computed/fixed column width):
`pad_left = (width - sprite_width) / 2` also goes negative and clamps to `0` (line 70-73) — centering is skipped entirely, the sprite prints left-aligned at its natural width. The right-pad calc (`rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)`) then also goes negative and clamps to `0`, so no extra right-padding is added either. This matches the documented behavior in the `POKEMON_WIDTH` comment: "if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered)." fastfetch then just starts the info text right after wherever that oversized sprite's widest line actually ends, plus whatever `POKEMON_GAP` (currently `0`) adds.

So in both cases it degrades gracefully rather than erroring — it just stops trying to center/align and falls back to flush-left placement.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Standalone demo of pokefetch's centering/padding logic using fake
# sprites instead of real pokeget output, so we can force the
# "too tall" and "too wide" cases on demand without touching the
# real script or needing a real oversized pokemon sprite.
set -euo pipefail

CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
POKEMON_GAP=0
FASTFETCH_CONFIG="$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc"

mode="$1"  # "tall" or "wide"
sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

if [[ "$mode" == "tall" ]]; then
    # Fake sprite: more rows than info text has (info_lines + 6),
    # each row narrow (5 cols) so width isn't also a factor.
    for i in $(seq 1 $((info_lines + 6))); do
        printf 'P%02d##\n' "$i"
    done > "$sprite"
else
    # Fake sprite: only 5 rows tall (fits fine), but each row is
    # 120 columns wide - much wider than the computed column width.
    for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        printf 'ROW%d-%s\n' "$i" "$(printf '#%.0s' $(seq 1 110))"
    done > "$sprite"
fi

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(awk '{ print length }' "$sprite" | sort -n | tail -1)

default_width=$(awk -v h="$info_lines" -v r="$CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", h * r + 0.5 }')
width="$default_width"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then pad_top=0; fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then pad_left=0; fi

echo "info_lines=$info_lines  sprite_lines=$sprite_lines  sprite_width=$sprite_width  column_width=$width"
echo "=> pad_top=$pad_top  pad_left=$pad_left"
echo "---------------------------------------------------------------"

awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-right "$POKEMON_GAP"

{

    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)

content.text:
Both ran against your real fastfetch config (24 info lines, ~60 column width) with fake sprites standing in for pokeget:

**Too tall** (`sprite_lines=30` vs `info_lines=24`): `pad_top` clamped to `0`. Rows `P01`–`P24` print alongside the info text as expected, then `P25`–`P30` (the last 6) just keep printing below it, on their own, once the info text runs out.

**Too wide** (`sprite_width=115` vs `column_width=60`): `pad_left` clamped to `0`, so centering is skipped — the sprite is flush left. And since it's wider than the whole info block is tall, only 5 of the 24 info rows actually have a sprite row next to them (rows 10–14 in the output); the rest of the info text prints with blank space on the left where the sprite would've been.

Full output is above if you want to scroll up and look at it directly. Demo script is at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/fe9e639d-58d6-4ce8-84a8-b4946f63a681/scratchpad/demo_padding.sh` if you want to rerun or tweak it — didn't touch your real pokefetch script.
